summary: A plumbing outfit whose reputation is carried by named people. The reviews are unusually strong and unusually specific, which is an asset most shops never build.

observations.title: Your crew is the brand
observations.detail: Brian, Mailo, Kayla, and Korey come up by name over and over across 93 reviews at a 4.9 average. Customers are not praising the company in the abstract, they are naming individuals.
observations.evidence: Multiple reviewers name specific technicians rather than the business.

observations.title: Most reviews never get a reply
observations.detail: Some reviews have a response from the shop and many do not. Consistent replies would show future customers that the business listens and give the team a visible place to add context when a review is critical.
observations.evidence: Owner responses appear on only a portion of the reviews read.

observations.title: A competitor-switch story is sitting unamplified
observations.detail: One reviewer describes leaving another plumbing company after a bad experience and being handled honestly here. That is the single most persuasive thing on the profile and nothing points to it.
observations.evidence: A detailed review describes switching after a poor experience elsewhere.

questions: How many calls come in during a job, when nobody can pick up?
Who replies to reviews right now, and how often?
When a customer asks for a specific tech, how do you handle it?
What happens to a quote request that arrives after hours?
focus: Replying to every review is the cheapest ranking win available here. What would it take to answer all 93, and keep up with new ones?
